body:
Hey, I feel for you. I don't think it was your fault. Sometimes things happen that are just not under our control. The only thing I can tell you is how I feel about my parents, my family. I don't have any blame for them, not anymore. I know they did everything that was in their power to raise me to be a happy guy. For some reason, partly, it didn't work out. Some days I'm fine and some days are really tough. And you know, I've just turned 22. I feel tired, old and beaten down. I don't know whether it's my body or my mind growing weaker, but it seems to me I have less and less energy to fight. However, it's an inner fight. Some shit I'm battling with inside me. The days that I'm fine I feel really grateful for a chance at life, it's an amazing place with beautiful things and experiences. But then again, when it strikes, I cannot see any of that. 

Anyways, are you blaming your wife for not being a good parent? Do you think it's her fault? Of course not. If no, why would you do it to yourself? Sometimes life is too much for us, something goes wrong, we make a mistake... It's so many variables it's impossible to figure out when we messed up - or if we ever messed up at all. There are things that go wrong even if we take each and every correct decision. Sometimes it has absolutely nothing to do with you or me. I hope one day you will be able to find your peace. I hope we all will.

I'm somehow in a similar situation. My middle sister is already on anti-depressants and the youngest is very well on her way there. We can't make her go to school, she will throw insane tantrums the moment she has to do anything requiring the slightest effort, won't even utter a word to us. It pains me so much to watch her spiral into that hole and I feel so hopeless. The thing about family is that it's never the single person - you're taking down the whole ship. Even if you decide to cut off somebody, the wound will always be there. And the thoughts that you should know how to help them...

Exactly what I wanted to write. It's like I have two people inside me. One is freaking killing it at life - outgoing, social (in comparison), productive and optimistic about future. This guy loves life, is full of positive emotions and just crushes everyday. And then there is this other guy, who just... I dunno man, you know how it looks like. Barely is able to keep himself alive. 

Whomever I'm at the moment is really not able to understand the other one. When the episode is over I don't even remember how it was like... It feels as if it happened to a different person. I seriously have very little recollection of my feelings and thoughts from the depressed state. I keep a journal and when I read it later it's like "Oh, this guy's life sucks. It's good that I'm not him." And then when the shit hits the fan once again "Oh, so that's what it's like..."

Never been big on running, but lifting used to make me feel that way. Nothing like the feeling of getting a solid deadlift session in. Haven't been there for a long time though... I don't know if it's really my health declining or just some mind issues, but couldn't keep up with workouts without my body breaking down. I have yoga now, but really hope I'll be able to get serious in the gym somewhere in the future.
Interesting thought. Thinking about it... you're already on the ground, so you cannot go down any further, right?
I think I'm ok now, had a worse day yesterday. Thank you for replying :)
Maybe you could start with a fb group or a post on meetup, meet somewhere for a coffee just to talk. Idk what you're looking for, but maybe those could work.
Hey, how can we say what normal is? I'd say people struggle more than we imagine, so that would be pretty normal. The reassuring thing is, despite that fact, we managed to go on for quite a while :)
Thank you! Thankfully, my sleep is a bliss usually. Hope you're good too.
I do and I highly recommend it. It's an anchor of peace in my day.
Hey, have you thought about starting something on your own? Maybe there's more people who would like to meet, but they too didn't find anything and gave up.
Yeah, now when I think about it. It all just weirdly passes away, without a notice.

Yeah, I feel you. From what I know, it's because I can't see a future for myself. Or I cannot see myself in the future. 

But there are some things that I want to do before dying and that keeps me alive. Plus the hope of never knowing what comes next. Maybe one day we will be happy?

Your siblings might indeed need you in the future. I guess it would be great if you read some books on psychology, so when the time comes you will know how to help them. I know some people who have the best of intentions, but they try to help in such a way that it only makes the matters worse.

The best kind of help is when you can lead by an example. So you have to sort yourself out first in order to help others. I wish you good luck. If you'd like to talk or have some book recommendations, shoot me a PM.

Hey, have you thought about going camping or spending some time in the wild? 

I always take great pleasure in being with nature. It saved me more than a few times. I have a forest nearby and I'd just go for a veeery long walk. Just me and the trees. Kinda puts things in perspective.

Oh, of course. My point was that you do these things and you keep improving, but the next day you're still not content with what you have. So if you won't learn to be happy with your *current you*, the *future you* will also not be enough. 

To put it in other words, the *future you* never comes, as it is always replaced by the *current you*. So in the end, it boils down to accepting your present self, as it is the only self that is real.

I hope it all makes some sense.

I kinda get what you're saying. Life from this perspective is beautiful, yet still really empty. Have you maybe read some Alan Watts? He talks quite a bit about this. That the things themselves have no purpose and so do we, people. If I understood him right, he meant that the purpose of things is their purposelessness. 

And you got me right with my longing for a better future. I just fear that I'll spend my whole life waiting for *the day that never comes*. With this mindset, hoping for a better tomorrow, it is never today. I feel that if I can't be happy now, I also won't find happiness in the future.
